answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake, slashed on proven fraud, and to earn trust only through repeated verifiable work. Like tending a garden, reputation grows slowly: newcomers start with tiny limits that rise only after honest trades accumulate. A sonnet of attestations from established peers helps, but endorsers must also stake their own standing. Forging identities then becomes ferrous in cost: every fake needs locked funds, time, and an endorser risking its stake, so a Sybil flood costs far more than it can earn.
